LESSON: PRONUNCIATION AND SPEAKING: FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1.1: Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should you speak accurately and without hesitations?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify words, phrases and sentences with the target sounds
2. use words and expressions such as idioms, proverbs and similes related to the theme in sentences correctly

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency

Teach
• Focus skill: identify words, phrases and sentences with the target sounds.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Pronunciation and Speaking: Fluency
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you speak accurately and without hesitations?
2. What is the importance of showing the right feelings when reciting a poem or telling a story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
